summary: Jacques Gernet was a scholar in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the universities of Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE. He held posts at the Sorbonne, EPHE, Paris Diderot University, and Collège de France (1975–1992).

Jacques Giès was a specialist in sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts and Paris-Sorbonne University under Flora Blanchon. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne and École du Louvre, and served as President of Guimet Museum (2008–2011).

Jacques Leider works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at INALCO, Paris-Sorbonne, and the University of Luxembourg, completing his doctorate under Denise Bernot. He taught at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) and joined the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2001.

Jacques Maritain was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Henri-IV, the Faculty of Arts of Paris, under Henri Bergson, and at the University of Notre Dame. He held a post at the University of Chicago (~1948–1953).

Jacques May specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Lausanne, Sorbonne, EPHE, and Collège de France, with doctoral supervisor Constantin Régamey. He held posts at EFEO, Hōbōgirin, and the University of Lausanne (1968; 1976–1992).

Jacques Scheuer was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau. He held posts at Centre Sèvres and taught as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain (~1977–2007).

Jacques van Ginneken was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. In 1923, he was appointed professor at the Catholic University of America and served at Radboud University Nijmegen from 1923 to 1945.

Jacques-Albert Cuttat worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the universities of Bern and Paris. His career included serving as Privatdozent at Bern (1935), teaching at Columbia University, and holding a professorship in philosophy at the Sorbonne.

Jadunath Sarkar was a historian who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He held faculty posts at Ripon College, Vidyasagar College, Patna College, BHU, Ravenshaw College, and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).
Jae-gwon Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Ryukoku University in 2007 and subsequently held a post there.
Jagaddhar Zadoo was an Indologist who worked in the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir, attested between 1924 and 1930, and serving as its Superintendent in 1947.

Jagadish Chandra Chatterji was an Indologist and philosopher who earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge. He served as Director of the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir, attested in 1911.

Jagannath Upadhyaya was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He was a professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1980–1983) and became the first director of the Rare Buddhist Text Research Project at CIHTS in 1985.

Jagdish Kashyap worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Patna College, BHU, and Vidyalankara Pirivena. He served as Professor of Pali at BHU and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and founded and directed the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jaideva Singh worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Swami Lakshman Joo, Srikrishna Harihirlekar, and Nankoo Bhaya Telang. He served as chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and Chairman of Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).

Jake H. Davis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Marlboro College, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and CUNY Graduate Center. He has taught at Brown University, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies, City College of New York, and NYU.
Jakob Bucher was an Indologist and linguist who served as a missionary for the Basel Mission and was Superintendent of the Anglo-Vernacular High School in 1890.
Jakob H. Thiessen was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Kiel University between 1875 and 1880 under the supervision of Richard Pischel.

Jakob Halfmann works in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held the Chair of Comparative Philology at the University of Würzburg (2023–2025) and became a Group Leader at the Free University of Berlin in 2026.

Jakob Hausheer studied at the University of Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler and Adolf Kaegi, and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Halle. In 1905, he became ordinary professor for Old Testament studies and Oriental languages at the University of Zurich.
